1.title: Supplementary Figure S1. Common measured ASD genes and conventional-T-cell context.
1.plain: Supplementary Figure S1. Common measured ASD genes and conventional-T-cell context. (a) Signed author log-fold changes (LFCs) and author-hit status for all 33 SFARI score-1 genes measured in both the Chen genome-wide human induced-Treg FOXP3 screen and the Umhoefer targeted screen. Each LFC cell shows the actual value rounded to two decimals; the common symmetric color scale covers all observed values. Filled and open circles denote author hits and measured nonhits. Shared numeric scales do not imply equivalent assay endpoints or biological effect directions. (b) Assay context: genome-wide discovery, independent primary-Treg support, and conventional-T-cell (Tconv) context. The targeted screen includes 1,349 mapped canonical targets, with two primary-Treg donors and three Tconv donors. (c) Tconv hit proportions are 4/33 ASD genes and 34/1,316 other measured genes; the frozen one-sided Fisher enrichment P is 0.0122. Tconv provides context and is not an independent Treg validation endpoint.

2.title: Supplementary Figure S2. Hit recalibration and influence sensitivity.
2.plain: Supplementary Figure S2. Hit recalibration and influence sensitivity. (a) Recalibrated enrichment and removal of the two shared hits, FOXP1 and ZMYND8, in Chen and primary Tregs. The recalibrated odds ratios (ORs) are 4.75 and 8.18, respectively, with one-sided Fisher P = 4.91 × 10⁻⁶ and 9.33 × 10⁻⁴. After removing both genes, ORs are 4.00 and 5.30, with P = 1.04 × 10⁻⁴ and 0.0269. Hit/measured counts are shown beneath the corresponding points. No confidence intervals were supplied for these estimates. (b) Recalibrated class-conditioned observed/expected hit ratios: Chen, 1.97; primary Treg, 2.86. The reference line is 1 on this separate metric axis. (c) All 242 Chen and 33 primary-Treg single-ASD-gene omission results, ordered alphabetically by the removed gene within each screen. Screen-colored points indicate removal of an author hit; gray points indicate removal of a nonhit. All omissions retain nominal one-sided Fisher P < 0.05. The dashed line marks that nominal reference. These analyses assess recalibration and influence sensitivity, not independent experimental replication.

3.title: Supplementary Figure S3. Regulator strata, joint coverage and mouse sensitivity.
3.plain: Supplementary Figure S3. Regulator strata, joint coverage and mouse sensitivity. (a) ASD and other-gene hit rates within the frozen operational regulator-class strata. Both denotes membership in the transcription-factor and EpiFactors catalogs; library in/out denotes membership in the targeted library for Chen. Filled and open bars represent ASD and other genes, respectively. Printed values give hits/measured in each stratum, preserving the small ASD denominators. Rates are K/A for ASD genes and (H - K)/(N - A) for other genes, using the released contingency cells. Catalog annotations do not establish pathway mechanisms. (b) Complete-case ASD coverage for joint class/expression/span/guide conditioning: Chen, 189/242 (78.1%); primary Treg, 22/33 (66.7%). (c) Mouse-screen sensitivity: primary OR = 1.13 with the supplied 95% display interval 0.529-2.13 and one-sided Fisher P = 0.405; fitness-sensitivity OR = 1.32 and P = 0.274, with no supplied interval. Class-conditioned O/E = 0.950 is displayed on its own axis, with exact one-sided P = 0.615. Mapping and assay differences limit cross-species equivalence.

4.title: Supplementary Figure S4. Whole-blood paired tests and descriptive Yan context.
4.plain: Supplementary Figure S4. Whole-blood paired tests and descriptive Yan context. (a) Program-score differences for 20 ASD-sibling family pairs in whole blood. Points and horizontal ranges show mean ASD-minus-sibling differences and the supplied conventional paired-t 95% display intervals. Exact P values are the frozen two-sided sign-flip tests; q values use Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment across the ten programs (BH10). The display intervals are not inversions of the sign-flip tests. The aligned bars show the counts of families with positive (navy, ASD > sibling) and negative (gray, ASD < sibling) score differences; all ten programs have zero ties. No program has BH10 q < 0.05. These family-level score differences do not estimate Treg abundance. (b) Fractions of M1-M10 programs present in the Yan Treg-like cluster T_CD4_c03_ANXA2_FOXP3 reported list (162 rows). Labels give listed-program-gene counts divided by fixed source-program sizes. The full tested universe and effect directions are unavailable, so these overlaps are descriptive and have no formal P or q. Whole-blood and reported-list context do not formally replicate purified-Treg evidence.

5.title: Supplementary Figure S5. Formal Moreno program inference and exact-ASD14 overlap.
5.plain: Supplementary Figure S5. Formal Moreno program inference and exact-ASD14 overlap. (a) Formal Moreno program inference uses five eligible programs within a fixed ten-program multiplicity family. Eligibility requires at least 20 measured program symbols and at least 70% source-membership coverage. The frozen asymptotic two-sided Mann-Whitney tests use tie and continuity correction. BH10 q values are M1, 3.37 × 10⁻¹⁷; M2, 0.488; M6, 5.74 × 10⁻⁴⁶; M8, 9.13 × 10⁻⁵; and M9, 4.05 × 10⁻⁸. M1, M6, M8 and M9 are supported; M2 is eligible but unsupported. M3, M4, M5, M7 and M10 are coverage-ineligible and receive no formal P or q. (b) Exact-ASD14 DEG overlap in Moreno is 0/14 (0%); other measured features contribute 288/5,837 (4.9%). The frozen Fisher enrichment OR is 0 and P is 1. The finite-effect universe contains 5,851 feature rows, without symbol deduplication. (c) All 14 ASD14 genes are measured in Moreno, but none is a DEG. Yan also has 0/14 queried-list overlap; its measured coverage is unavailable, and that denominator is a query set. Exact-gene overlap and program-level support are distinct endpoints in the single purified-Treg dataset.
